# Texas eyes the SEC title game, but a desperate Texas A&M awaits on Friday

COLLEGE STATION, Texas -- — A year ago, the undefeated Texas A&M Aggies needed a win over Texas in the regular-season finale to clinch a spot in the Southeastern Conference title game.

The Aggies left Austin with a 27-17 loss and missed the chance to make the title game for the first time in program history.

This year it’s the fifth-ranked Longhorns who have a shot to reach the conference championship game and are heading for the College Football Playoff. They’ll need some help — they have to beat their archrival on Friday night for a fourth straight time to have a chance to face top-ranked Georgia in Atlanta on Dec. 5.

“They just want to beat us and hurt our game, what we are trying to do this season,” Texas defensive lineman Lance Jackson said. “Last year we wanted to beat them because they could have gone to the SEC championship, so our goal was to beat them and hurt what they had going on and vice versa this year, they are trying to beat us and hurt what we have going on.”

That is virtually all the Aggies have left to play for as they wrap up a miserable season a year after reaching the CFP for the first time. Texas A&M enters the game having lost four in a row and with only four wins, Friday will be the team’s final game regardless of the outcome.

“Nothing’s going to erase what has happened,” Texas A&M coach Mike Elko said. “Nothing is going to change the results and the need to show massive improvement and fix where we’re at right now. But not everybody gets this opportunity to play a game this meaningful when you’ve had the season that we’ve had.”

Added Jackson: “We know they don’t get to play in a bowl game this year, so this is like their bowl game.”
